headline_drivers: Record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $93.1M (+219% YoY) with $32.1M gross operating margin and positive adjusted EBITDA, driven by expanded Bitcoin mining and growing BUZZ HPC/AI cloud revenue (company press release, 2026-05-20; Q3 call transcript, 2026-05-20)

Explicit strategic pivot and reiterated target to reach $225M annual recurring revenue from BUZZ high‑performance computing GPU cloud by year‑end, with plans to expand to ~11,000 GPUs and convert a Tier 3 New Brunswick data center for AI/HPC workloads (Q3 FY2026 press release and earnings call, 2026-05-20)

Uplisting from TSX Venture Exchange to Toronto Stock Exchange and concurrent ATM equity raise of ~15M shares for $41.1M gross proceeds, improving liquidity and funding AI/HPC expansion (Form 8‑K / company disclosure and TSX announcement, effective 2026-05-12)

Earlier FY2026 quarters showed sequential record revenue (Q1 FY2026: $45.6M; Q2 FY2026: record revenue with 285% YoY growth and 48.6% gross margin), establishing a trend of rapid top‑line acceleration alongside increasing Bitcoin hashrate and BUZZ HPC growth (company press releases, 2025-08-14 for Q1 FY2026; 2025-11-XX for Q2 FY2026)

Crypto/AI ‘dual‑beta’ narrative attracting active traders: media and trading‑desk commentary highlight HIVE as a turnaround/high‑volatility AI‑and‑Bitcoin play with low debt and strong liquidity, drawing in momentum and day‑trading flows (StocksToTrade note, 2026-05-19)

Announcement of a large AI infrastructure ‘sovereign AI gigafactory’ project in the Greater Toronto Area via subsidiary BUZZ High Performance Computing, framed as a major AI data-center buildout (reported May 18, 2026)

Cantor Fitzgerald raises HIVE price target from $3.00 to $4.60 and reiterates Overweight, explicitly valuing the AI/cloud segment on 2027 revenues and highlighting >$3B potential ARR if the Ontario site is fully contracted (May 19, 2026)

HIVE completes graduation to the main Toronto Stock Exchange, improving institutional visibility and perceived credibility as it pivots from pure crypto mining to AI/HPC infrastructure (effective May 19, 2026)

Strong recent quarterly results with revenue of ~$93M in FQ3 2025, up ~219% YoY, and positive adjusted EBITDA of $5.7M, reinforcing that the business is scaling as both Bitcoin hashrate and HPC ramp (reported in the latest quarterly update, within the last 60 days)
summary:
A focused verification search did not uncover any marquee buyer wins or hidden supply‑chain catalysts for HIVE Digital Technologies in the past 60–90 days. Specifically: there are no reports or credible rumors that Apple, NVIDIA, TSMC, Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, Tesla, OpenAI, Anthropic, major auto OEMs, or defense primes have adopted, qualified, or begun mass‑producing with HIVE’s infrastructure. No Ming‑Chi Kuo, DigiTimes, Wedbush, Loop Capital, Needham, or Morgan Stanley supply‑chain notes mentioning HIVE were found in this window. Likewise, there are no disclosed design wins, qualification events, or roadmap‑specific AI/HPC contracts tying HIVE’s BUZZ GPU cloud or data centers to a named blue‑chip anchor customer, nor any patent filings or conference disclosures that clearly imply such a relationship.

The identifiable fundamental drivers behind the stock’s recent move are instead company‑specific but non–marquee‑customer in nature: (1) very strong reported financial momentum culminating in record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $93.1M (+219% YoY) with a sharply higher $32.1M gross operating margin and positive adjusted EBITDA, driven mainly by expanded Bitcoin mining and improving efficiency; (2) management’s explicit emphasis on its BUZZ high‑performance computing and AI cloud strategy, including a stated goal of reaching $225M ARR from HPC by year‑end and scaling to roughly 11,000 GPUs by converting a Tier 3 New Brunswick facility, which reframes HIVE from a pure crypto miner to an AI/HPC infrastructure play; and (3) the May 12, 2026 uplisting from TSX Venture to the main Toronto Stock Exchange, plus an at‑the‑market equity raise of ~15M shares for $41.1M, boosting both institutional visibility and balance‑sheet capacity to fund AI/HPC build‑out.

These elements, together with earlier FY2026 quarters showing record revenue and margin expansion and with trading‑desk commentary positioning HIVE as a high‑beta way to play both AI infrastructure and a recovering crypto cycle, appear to be the primary catalysts. The verification pass therefore refines the explanation toward a fundamentals‑driven re‑rating around growth, margins, and strategic repositioning, amplified by technical/momentum flows, rather than any single undisclosed or marquee‑customer contract win. No hidden big‑name buyer catalyst could be substantiated in the recent record.
